symptom: Items whose stated category was contradicted by several independent structural checks nonetheless summarized as mild. The contradicting checks had all run and all disagreed; each disagreement was then recorded as expected, so the summary showed one unresolved tension where there were four. Nothing in the output indicated that the classification of those disagreements as expected was itself a consequence of a correction the same system had applied moments earlier.
mechanism_as_described: A correction stage overwrote the item's computed category with a different one. Separately, the summary that assembles disagreements from the diagnostic subsystems suppresses those known to be normal for the category the item holds — a sensible rule, since some subsystems characteristically disagree with certain categories. But the category they were tested against was the corrected one. The correction had moved the item into precisely the category in which a structural second-classness and a descent failure ARE normal, so the disagreements arrived pre-explained and were filed rather than raised. Remove the correction, and the original category returns; the same unchanged disagreements are then abnormal for it and surface as genuine. The summary moves from mild to severe with no measurement changed and no change to the item's stated category. The suppression rule was never about the evidence — it was keyed to a category the system had assigned to itself.
detection_path: Running the full comparison before and after removing the correction over an identical working set, and requiring every unaffected item to come out byte-identical — which isolated the three affected items and made the change in their summaries attributable to the correction and nothing else. The decisive step was that the change ran contrary to what had been written down in advance: a milder summary was predicted and a stronger one arrived, and the discrepancy was investigated instead of accepted. Generality was then established across five working sets totalling roughly six thousand items: all eighty-two affected items carried the same structural disagreements, so the three were not special.
consequence: For as long as the correction was in place, items whose stated category was structurally contradicted reported the contradiction as expected and summarized mild. The concealment is self-reinforcing: the more decisively the correction moves an item, the more completely the evidence against it is classified as normal. From any output, a genuinely mild case and a suppressed severe one are indistinguishable — the same summary colour, the same conflicts listed as expected. The corrected behaviour makes those items report severe, which reads as a regression and is the opposite: it is what the correction had been hiding.

extraction_notes.unit_is_incident_not_audit: The unit describes the defect the conversion exposed, not the conversion.
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: Four separable incidents here. Two were close on described-mechanism depth (the extracted one and the query-form bypass below), so the tiebreak was the rule already applied in this packet: prefer the incident that ACTUALLY OCCURRED and had a realized consequence over one caught before it mattered. The extracted defect held for the correction's entire life across every affected item in five working sets; the bypass produced two wrong members in one sweep and was caught there.
alternatives_not_extracted: A priority chain terminated by cuts returns exactly one winner per item when queried with the result UNBOUND. Queried with the result BOUND to a specific value, head unification reaches the matching clause without passing through the earlier clauses' cuts, so the query succeeds whenever that clause's detector fires — even when a higher-priority clause is the true winner. A membership test written the natural way therefore returns a superset, and every count taken that way overstates. Witnessed: one sweep in this same directory over-included two items, and the counts in a sibling document had to be re-derived in the unbound form. Real, occurred, and fully described — the strongest alternative.

A firing count was being read as an impact measure. Of fifty items where one correction was the winner, only three had their category actually changed; on the other forty-seven the correction's input pattern did not match and it silently returned the input unchanged. The headline 'forty-one fires' overstated the blast radius by more than an order of magnitude. NOT extracted because it is described as a measurement correction made during the evidence pass rather than as a defect that produced a wrong result downstream.

A trap averted rather than suffered: the natural way to grade the severity of a converted correction is by the size of the category change, which after conversion is always zero — so a severity that should have stayed high would have silently dropped to advisory on every converted item. It was anticipated and graded on an independent discriminant instead, with a two-sided control witnessing that the discriminant does the work. NOT extracted because it never occurred.
